title: Free a stuck pickle jar lid with a lifter tool, then twist it off while the other hand holds the jar
instruction: Open the pickle jar and set the lid down.
context: Opening a stuck jar is a firsthand everyday experience. A stuck vacuum-sealed lug lid will not turn until a spoon, jar key or church key is slid under its edge and lifted; once it turns it spins the jar on the counter unless a second hand holds the jar. Unlike RLBench open_jar and Bi-DexHands BottleCap (unsealed lid, no tool, no jar reaction), the merged child-resistant-cap task (no seal, no jar reaction) and PR #922 (paint-tin lever: a straight prise, no turn, no holding hand), the lid here stays locked until a tool has lifted its edge, and then needs a counter-torque.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left, table top 74.75 cm). Glass pickle jar: body 7.8 cm across and 10.5 cm tall to the shoulder ledge, neck 6.5 cm across and 1.7 cm tall (glass top 12.2 cm), 0.65 kg in total (0.25 kg glass, 0.40 kg pickles and brine fused to the jar), friction 0.45, centre x 22, y 0. Gold lug lid: 7.0 cm across, 2.1 cm tall, 0.03 kg, friction 0.9, bottom edge 11.5 cm above the table (1 cm above the ledge), on the jar. Steel and ABS lever tool: 12.5 x 2.4 cm steel blade 2 mm thick, an orange 10 x 1 x 4 cm ABS grip fin on the blade, 0.091 kg, friction 0.6, lying flat at x 34, y -14, tip toward +y (the jar).
scoring: Scored on the end state; 1.0 only after everything holds 20 consecutive steps (1 s). 0 if the jar tilts more than 30 degrees at any step once the lid is unlatched (brine at the rim; the headspace allows 37 degrees) or leaves the table. 0.25 seal broken (latched): lever blade tip 2.8-3.8 cm from the jar axis (under the lid skirt), at ledge height up to 2 mm above the lid's raised bottom edge, pointing at the jar within 35 degrees, with the lid edge raised at least 1 mm by it, for 5 steps; hovering near the rim earns nothing. 0.5 lid unlatched (turned 80 degrees relative to the jar counter-clockwise seen from above, the loosening way; a tightening turn never unlatches; latched) and its centre within 5 cm of the jar axis. 0.75 lid centre 5 cm or more from the jar axis but held, in the air, moving or not yet down. 1.0 lid unlatched and flat on the table (centre height 6.5 to 14.5 mm), 10.4 cm or more from the jar axis (30 mm clear of the jar footprint), lid and jar still (< 0.005 m/s, jar < 0.1 rad/s), jar tilt at most 10 degrees and within 6 cm of its start, both grippers open and at least 7 cm from the jar axis and the lid centre. The clockwise stop is soft: the lid can be turned clockwise, but that never unlatches it or scores above 0.25.
reset_notes: Sealed jar upright at its start pose, lid on, lever tool flat at its start pose, tip toward the jar.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, no air or liquid. The lid stays jointed to the jar (cannot tip, flip or hit it); the vacuum seal is a latch in task logic: locked (30 N m, estimate) until a blade under the lid edge raises it 1 mm for 5 steps. Then the lug lid turns against 0.4 N m (estimate); only 80 deg counter-clockwise (loosening) unlatches it. The clockwise stop is soft: it turns but never unlatches or scores above 0.25. Pickles and brine: one 0.40 kg mass in the 0.65 kg jar. Lid friction 0.9, glass 0.45.
